samples.summary: 'removeLink leaves a link the selection does not touch' may pass vacuously — it never asserts a selection actually formed
samples.evidence: The test calls `pressShiftLeft(3)` (three synthetic `keydown` ArrowLeft+shift events) and then asserts only `inlines.some(i => i.style.href === '…')`. Nothing asserts that a selection exists after the key presses (no `api`-level selection read, and `text-box-editor.ts` has no `ArrowLeft` handling of its own — grep for `ArrowLeft` in `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts` returns nothing, so this depends entirely on the shared TextEditor keydown path being wired through this harness). If no selection forms, `removeLink()` falls into the caret branch with the caret at the end of 'now', `findLinkRunAt` returns nothing, and the assertion holds regardless of whether the new selection branch over-reaches. The complementary test at line 168 does discriminate, so the gap is only in the over-reach guard.

samples.summary: The mobile toolbar's new `showRemoveLink` opt-in has no test, while the desktop sibling opt-in does
samples.evidence: `text-edit-section.tsx`'s opt-in is asserted at the call site by `remove-link-button.test.ts` ('the Slides text-edit toolbar opts in'), with an explicit rationale that an optional prop never passed 'fails silently — no type error, no runtime error, just a surface with no way to remove a link'. The identical opt-in added in `mobile-toolbar.tsx:580` (TextFormatSheet) has no such assertion: grepping `showRemoveLink` / `Remove link` across packages/frontend/tests only matches `remove-link-button.test.ts`, and `tests/app/slides/toolbar/mobile-text-toggles.test.ts` does not reference the button. On mobile Slides this button is the only path to drop a hyperlink, so a silent regression there is invisible.

samples.summary: The `prev.href === undefined` re-arm disjunct (both in `pendingStyleFor` and `TextEditor.clearFormatting`) is never exercised independently of `isAtLinkTrailingEdge`
samples.evidence: Both new guards are `isAtLinkTrailingEdge(...) || !!(prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined)`. Every new test that reaches them (`link-trailing-edge.test.ts` 'Cmd+\\ at a link trailing edge…', 'the Clear formatting button at a link trailing edge…', the Bold and font-size cases) does `editor.insertLink(...)` and leaves the caret at the link's trailing edge, so the first disjunct is already true — the second can be deleted without failing any test. The mirrored code at `text-editor.ts:3441-3442` has the same gap. Impact is contained (it is a belt-and-braces re-arm), but the branch is asserted nowhere.

samples.summary: The Cmd+\ keyset-drift fix is only partly asserted: only `color` is checked, not `fontSize`, `fontFamily` or `backgroundColor`
samples.evidence: The docstring says the shortcut's hand-rolled list 'omitted `fontSize`, `fontFamily`, `color` and `backgroundColor`'. The only new shortcut test, `editor-clear-formatting.test.ts` 'the Mod+\\ shortcut keeps the hyperlink too' (line ~180), asserts `href`, `bold` and `color` — the fixture (`linkedBlock`) carries no `fontSize`, `fontFamily` or `backgroundColor` at all, so three of the four newly-cleared keys are untested for the shortcut path. The collapsed-caret shortcut path likewise never asserts the newly-added keys land on the next typed run (the link tests only assert `href`/text).

samples.summary: 'a collapsed-caret clear at a link trailing edge keeps the link intact' cannot fail on this diff — the path it exercises is a no-op before and after
samples.evidence: `text-box-editor.ts:823` `applyStyleImpl` returns immediately when there is no selection, and `clearInlineFormatting` (line 1081) just calls it — so at a collapsed caret the call does nothing, both with and without this change (the change is only the removal of `href` from `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE`, which never reaches a run here). The test's own comment concedes this ('it stages nothing at a collapsed caret'). It is a valid non-regression guard for the pre-existing `exitLinkIfAtTrailingEdge` machinery, but it is not coverage of anything this diff changes.

samples.summary: `pendingStyleFor`'s `'href' in style` early return (an explicit href write wins over the trailing-edge exit) has no test and no found caller
samples.evidence: The branch is justified by the comment as protecting `insertLink`, but `EditorAPI.insertLink` does not route through `applyStyleImpl` and a repo-wide grep for `applyStyle({ href` / `applyStyle({href` returns no matches. No test in `link-trailing-edge.test.ts` or `editor-clear-formatting.test.ts` calls `applyStyle` with an `href` key, so the branch is unexercised; if it were wrong (e.g. inverted) nothing would fail.

mergedFrom.summary: New Remove-link toolbar button has no test at all, yet the diff argues it is the only way to drop a hyperlink in Slides

finding.summary: New Remove-link toolbar button (showRemoveLink) has no test at all, though it is now the only way to drop a hyperlink in Slides
finding.evidence: The diff adds a `showRemoveLink` prop, an `IconUnlink` ToolbarButton (aria-label "Remove link") and a `handleRemoveLink` callback in text-format-group.tsx, and opts it in from `text-edit-section.tsx` and `mobile-toolbar.tsx`. No test asserts (a) the button renders only when `showRemoveLink` is passed, (b) clicking it calls `editor.removeLink()` and re-focuses. `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts` already provides exactly the needed jsdom + createRoot + `[aria-label=...]` harness for TextFormatGroup, so such a test was cheap; `tests/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.test.ts` only does state-machine checks plus a module-import smoke test (`expect(typeof mod.TextEditSection).toBe("function")`) and merely stubs `removeLink: () => {}`. Since Clear formatting no longer removes hyperlinks (#1051) and slides has no link popover, a silently unrendered or unwired button leaves users with no way to remove a link, and nothing in CI would catch it (frontend has no tsc, and JSX props like a typo'd/never-passed flag fail silently).

verdict.reason: A dedicated test suite for exactly the allegedly untested behavior exists at packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/remove-link-button.test.ts. It covers both claims the finding says are unasserted: (a) the button renders only when the prop is passed — "is not rendered by default" asserts the aria-label query is null while asserting the sibling "Insert link" button IS present so the selector is not dead (lines 74-82), and "is rendered when showRemoveLink is passed" (lines 84-89); and (b) clicking it asserts editor.removeLink was called exactly once AND editor.focus was called, plus a negative assertion that clearInlineFormatting was not called (lines 91-106). It further covers the disabled state (108-125) and, crucially, the silent-flag risk the finding centers on: it imports the real src/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx, renders it, finds the button and clicks it, asserting the real call site opts in and reaches removeLink (127-152). The assertions match the implementation at text-format-group.tsx:174-178 (handleRemoveLink calls editor.removeLink then editor.focus) and 310-325 (showRemoveLink-guarded ToolbarButton with aria-label "Remove link" and IconUnlink). The file is genuinely executed rather than orphaned: vite.config.ts:375-380 includes "tests/**/*.test.ts", which matches its path. The vi.fn() editor is the injected collaborator, not the unit under test, so this is not over-mocking — the real component's render guard and click wiring are exercised. The reviewer's reported empty grep for showRemoveLink/removeLink under packages/frontend is contradicted by the repository; that grep hits this test file six times.

finding.summary: Text-box `clearInlineFormatting` collapsed-caret-at-link-trailing-edge case is untested (and lacks the override the docs path got)
finding.evidence: `TextBoxEditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` still calls `applyStyleImpl(CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE)` with no trailing-edge `href: undefined` override — the addition the diff made only to `EditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting` (editor.ts:3366) and `TextEditor.clearFormatting`. The new test file `packages/docs/test/view/text-box-clear-formatting.test.ts` only covers a select-all range clear and `removeLink`; it never places a collapsed caret at a link's trailing edge, clears, and types. The docs counterpart deems exactly that scenario a defect ('the next typed character would silently extend the link') and covers it in link-trailing-edge.test.ts, but the slides/text-box equivalent (`text-box-link-trailing-edge.test.ts` covers only Space/Enter) has no such case, so link extension via the Slides Clear-formatting button ships with no coverage.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists. packages/docs/test/view/text-box-clear-formatting.test.ts:197-214 ("a collapsed-caret clear at a link trailing edge keeps the link intact") places a collapsed caret at the link's trailing edge (insertLink moves the cursor to pos.offset + url.length, text-box-editor.ts:1231), calls api.clearInlineFormatting() (line 206), then types (' ' and 'now', lines 207-208), and asserts the typed tail did not inherit the href: inlines[0].style.href === 'https://example.com' and the last inline's href is falsy (lines 212-213), plus full text integrity (line 211). Those assertions fail precisely under the "next typed character silently extends the link" defect the finding says is uncovered, so it is meaningful, not vacuous. The finding's code-side premise is also wrong in a way that removes the gap: TextBoxEditorAPI.clearInlineFormatting delegates to applyStyleImpl (text-box-editor.ts:1081-1086), which early-returns when there is no selection (line 824), so no caret pending style is seeded and no href override is needed — unlike TextEditor.clearFormatting, which does stage pending at a collapsed caret and therefore required the re-arm (text-editor.ts:3426-3450). The reviewer's reported empty grep for 'clearFormatting|clearInlineFormatting' under packages/docs/test does not reproduce; the same search returns this file.
